findings.location: definition_of_done.criterion (all four); contract.shapes 'reaching the guarantee...' (xc-compensation); contract.shapes.entry-conformance-report... audit-trail-implement's entry_kinds_seen enum
findings.finding: Every machine-checkable proof in this batch that a cross-cutting guarantee is applied 'whichever entry point was used' (T2.3) is scoped to TARGET T1's three ways in (human, agent, event) and never asserts coverage of TARGET T6.2's fourth, distinct entry, schedule. composable-plan.md section 3.4 states the two enumerations are not the same set: Time (schedule) 'Starts only' and carries its own identity/money ('whoever registered the schedule' / 'a standing allocation'), while T1's 'event' maps to the Internal door, which 'steers only'. A scheduled root run therefore has no T1 analogue at all, yet none of these four skills' definitions of done exercise it: xc-enforcement-chain's tool takes `--ways-in human,agent,event`; xc-compensation's shape even shows a fourth worked example under a schedule actor but its own definition_of_done asserts only `ways_in_covered == 3`; xc-audit-trail's criterion asserts 'entry_kinds_seen contains all three of TARGET T1's ways in' while its own scan is itself schedule-triggered; and xc-audit-trail-implement's entry_kinds_seen schema enum lists 'schedule' as a legal value that no assertion ever requires be present.
findings.evidence: xc-enforcement-chain definition_of_done.criterion: "--corpus out/units.jsonl --points admission,dispatch,call --ways-in human,agent,event --min-units 100". xc-compensation contract.shapes[1].examples[0][3]: {"way_in": "a recurrence fires (the fourth entry of the consumption reference, same shape)", "in": {"actor": {"subject": "schedule:nightly-fault-sweep"}...}} directly followed by xc-compensation.definition_of_done.criterion asserting only "ways_in_covered == 3". xc-audit-trail definition_of_done.criterion: "that `entry_kinds_seen` contains all three of TARGET T1's ways in, and that `independent` and `scheduled` were read from what the scan actually ran under". xc-audit-trail-implement contract.shapes[1].properties.entry_kinds_seen.items.enum: ["user", "agent", "service", "schedule"], with definition_of_done.criterion never asserting on that field at all. docs/reference/composable-plan.md section 3.4: "Four entries cover nearly every situation: a human, an event, a schedule (time), and an external system or agent... Time (schedule) | Starts only | ... a standing allocation".
findings.suggested_change: For each of the four skills, widen the conformance proof from three ways in to T6.2's four: xc-enforcement-chain's tool gains a fourth `--ways-in` value and asserts `ways_in==4` alongside `points_covered`; xc-compensation's definition_of_done asserts `ways_in_covered == 4` (the shape already has the fourth worked example to test against); xc-audit-trail's and xc-audit-trail-implement's criteria assert `entry_kinds_seen` contains `schedule` in addition to the three T1 kinds, since the schema already declares it. Where a schedule-originated root run cannot yet be produced in this environment, record the gap as an open_question with the 1-3-1 default (proposed) rather than leaving the assertion silently narrower than what the shape or schema already promises.

findings.location: composes_with.builds_on; contract.invariants stating the dispatch/call/step-boundary placement
findings.finding: xc-enforcement-chain is the skill that names itself 'the single structure' cross-cutting concerns attach to and explicitly invites this: its description says load it 'when a new concern needs somewhere to attach'. Three guarantee skills and the entry-conformance suite each independently assert the identical placement claim the chain formalizes - applied at the dispatch boundary and/or the call boundary, checked by value rather than by presence - without citing the chain, naming which of its six slots (identity.resolve, policy.decide, budget.reserve, telemetry.open, idempotency.claim, provenance.open) their own attachment corresponds to, or appearing in its used_by list (docs/skill-manifest.json: xc-enforcement-chain.used_by == ['xc-enforcement-chain-implement', 'xc-tenancy'] only). This is architecturally explicable by wave order (xc-compensation and xc-audit-trail are wave 6, xc-enforcement-chain is wave 7) for two of the four, but build-entry-conformance is wave 8, authored after the chain existed, and still does not cite it. The result is two unlinked places asserting 'applied by the platform at the dispatch boundary' in different vocabulary, which is exactly the compose-by-name gap this repository's own ceremony history (ceremony 2, 3, 4 lessons) repeatedly found and fixed for single facts; here it recurs for a whole placement claim.
findings.evidence: xc-enforcement-chain.description: "Load it when...a new concern needs somewhere to attach". xc-compensation.contract.invariants (guarantee-applied-by-platform row): "The guarantee is applied by the platform at the dispatch boundary and again at every step boundary, never requested by a caller" (sources: F-b1-08, F-b4-01 - no xc-enforcement-chain citation anywhere in the file). xc-audit-trail.contract.invariants (design-rule-7 row): "there is no audit call, no audit flag and no exempt list: the trail is derived from the ledger, identity, provenance and correlation records the platform already writes" (same F-b1-08/F-b4-01 citation, no chain reference). build-entry-conformance.instructions[2]: "Assert the per-door attachments by value: the delegation hop count and the subject prefix expected for that door, and the budget source...on the entry record and on every step record beneath it" - this is a direct check on the identity.resolve and budget.reserve slots xc-enforcement-chain declares, cited to X-entry-composition-059/T-t2-03 only. `grep -rl 'enforcement-chain' xc-compensation xc-audit-trail xc-audit-trail-implement build-entry-conformance` returns nothing.
findings.suggested_change: Add xc-enforcement-chain to the builds_on of xc-compensation, xc-audit-trail, xc-audit-trail-implement and build-entry-conformance (and add each in turn to xc-enforcement-chain's used_by in both the skill.json and docs/skill-manifest.json), with one invariant per skill naming which named point (admission/dispatch/call) and which slot(s) its own check rides on - e.g. xc-compensation's declare_effect binds at the dispatch/step boundary the chain also names, and build-entry-conformance's per-door identity/budget assertion is a check on the identity.resolve and budget.reserve slots specifically.

findings.finding: The measured evidence sentence describes the byte flipped in the ledger-verify breakage test as 'an actor name, opus-improver to opus-improvor', but kb/ledger.jsonl's field for that value is named `agent`, not `actor` - the entry-shape schema this same skill and xc-audit-trail define elsewhere uses `actor` for a different, not-yet-built field. Re-run confirms the underlying measurement is still accurate (`python3 tools/kb.py ledger-verify` currently reports 17 records, chain intact, up from the 16 recorded at measurement time, consistent with one more ceremony record having been appended since), but the prose could mislead a reader checking the claim against the file into looking for a field that is not there under that name.
findings.evidence: adapters[0].maps_to: "flipping one character inside the eighth historical record (an actor name, opus-improver to opus-improvor)". kb/ledger.jsonl line 8 (record L-00008): {"agent": "opus-improver", ...} - no `actor` key present in the record at all.
findings.suggested_change: Reword to 'an agent name' or 'the agent field' to match kb/ledger.jsonl's actual key, so the sentence stays checkable by grepping the file it describes.

findings.finding: xc-enforcement-chain's description shares two multi-word trigger phrases near-verbatim with xc-policy-gate's: both say 'rather than what it decides' immediately after naming where a decision/guarantee is applied, and both list 'someone proposes a fast path' as a trigger clause. Given xc-enforcement-chain's dispatch/call points are where xc-policy-gate's decision is consulted, some co-triggering is probably intended (a fast-path proposal should likely load both), but the phrase-level duplication is the kind of restated-fact pattern the repo's compose-by-name convention flags elsewhere, and neither description says the other owns the underlying rule.
findings.evidence: xc-enforcement-chain.description: "Load it when asking where a cross-cutting guarantee is actually applied rather than what it decides...when someone proposes a fast path, a trusted caller or a per-team exemption". xc-policy-gate.description: "Load it when deciding where a refusal is consulted rather than what it decides...when someone proposes a fast path, an advisory mode or a warn-only rollout for a ch[eck]".
findings.suggested_change: If the overlap is deliberate co-triggering, no change needed beyond noting it; if not, narrow one of the two 'fast path' clauses (e.g. xc-enforcement-chain's to 'a fast path around a whole point' versus xc-policy-gate's 'a fast path around one decision') so a reader can tell which skill a given fast-path proposal should load first.
